stop_status: REPAIRED - one medium memory-safety defect (out-of-bounds write from an over-weight hint, ASan-confirmed on the pre-fix body), one low out-of-bounds/UB class (zero-polynomial hint decode), and two low checked-extent repairs were found and fixed. No further memory-safety defect was found. FAST, BATCH and the targeted ASan controls pass. Nothing is promoted to SAFETY_DISCHARGED or SAFE_COMPATIBLE.

authority.source: openssl-3.6.4 (forensics/authorities/src/openssl-3.6.4/crypto/ml_dsa/ml_dsa_encoders.c), cross-checked line by line against the crate body
authority.abi: C ABI unchanged: no export, signature, #[repr(C)] layout, CRYPTO_* seam coordinate (file/line pairs 629/644/650/692/716/744/750/773/809) or unsafe lint attribute changed. The repairs are local bounds, refused arms and documentation.
external_contracts: The ML-DSA key object is internal. Its unsafe entry points require a live MlDsaKey in the state its constructors produce: encoded members are NULL or live allocations owned by the key (plain seam for pub_encoding, secure seam for priv_encoding/seed, each of the parameter set's exact length), and t1/s1 sub-allocations satisfy the vector invariants.

ossl_ml_dsa_sk_decode may receive the key's own priv_encoding as in_ (the explicit-key load path). On a public-hash mismatch it resets the key, which releases that buffer; the caller must not use in_ afterwards.

A hostile wire input is a (ptr,len) pair whose len equals the parameter set's pk_len/sk_len/sig_len; every field read is bounds-checked against it by Packet::get_bytes. A length mismatch is refused before any pointer is dereferenced.

The hint vector in a signature object is in-memory state, not wire input. FIPS 204 requires at most omega set coefficients; the signing caller establishes it with vector_count_ones and hint_bits_decode re-establishes it for decoded signatures. The encoder now refuses a violation locally instead of relying on that caller.

A caller-installed CRYPTO_set_mem_functions/secure-heap observer must see each allocation and release at the authority's own coordinates; the local OwnedBuf carries the allocation kind, extent and both coordinate pairs.
No safe Rust caller reaches any raw operation in this file: the OwnedBuf constructors are the only safe entry points and they fix the release extent from the allocation.

boundaries.mechanism: file-local OB-1 OwnedBuf over CRYPTO_malloc / CRYPTO_secure_malloc and CRYPTO_secure_clear_free, plus into_raw transfer
residuals: The safe constructors fix len to the requested allocation extent and Drop is the single release, so no safe caller can manufacture a cleansing length above the block (the OB-1 invariant).

The secure arm is verified separately: with no secure heap CRYPTO_secure_malloc falls back to the plain seam, and CRYPTO_secure_clear_free recognises the non-secure provenance, cleanses exactly len bytes and releases through CRYPTO_free. runtime::secure's clear_free/fallback/zero-length tests witness this seam.
into_raw is file-private and is called only on the success branch after the old member has been released; no safe path exposes an untracked block.
There is no adoption constructor: every block in this unit comes from a constructor call in the same function, so provenance is not re-asserted by hand (AGENTS §1).

boundaries.mechanism: pkEncode/pkDecode: public-key serialisation, CRYPTO_memdup cache, old-member replacement, failure ownership
residuals: pkDecode refuses a key whose encoded members are non-NULL, then allocates t1 and caches the public-key hash; an early refusal leaves the allocated public members owned by the key (authority parity, freed by key_reset/key_free).
On success the member is a fresh plain-seam CRYPTO_memdup block; on a memdup refusal the member stays NULL and the call reports 0.
pkEncode frees the incumbent pub_encoding only after the whole encoding lands, at the authority's :644 coordinate.

boundaries.mechanism: skEncode/skDecode: secret-key serialisation, secure scratch block, seed cleanse, priv_encoding ownership and the in_ alias path
residuals: skEncode allocates the scratch block on the secure seam, cleanses it on every failure arm (secure_clear_free at :750) and releases the incumbent priv_encoding at :744 before transferring the new block.
skDecode cleanses and releases key->seed at :773 before any refusal, decoded s1/s2/t0 live in the key's secure block (cleansed by key_reset), and the fresh priv_encoding copy is secure.

When priv_encoding == in_ the function does not re-copy; a subsequent public-hash mismatch resets the key and therefore releases in_. This is the authority's explicit-key load path and is now stated in the contract.
Early decode refusals (header, packet, trailing bytes) leave the key partially populated but entirely owned; the authority does the same and the eventual reset/free cleanses the secret vectors.

boundaries.mechanism: twelve bit-packing primitives and their byte-order/load-store helpers plus packet_copy_bytes
residuals: Every decode read goes through Packet::get_bytes, so a truncated packet is refused before the fixed-width load; every encode write is preceded by WPACKET_allocate_bytes at the exact width the loop stores.
The coefficient loops use fixed iteration counts that match 256 coefficients (32x8, 64x4, 64x2) and never index past the Poly array.
packet_copy_bytes requires destination writability and disjointness; every caller passes a key array of at least the copied fixed size.
The encoder now refuses the (omega+1)th set coefficient instead of writing it; the authority writes past the omega+k packet (UB) in that state.
The decoder refuses a zero-polynomial vector; the authority's do/while runs once for k == 0, reading past the limit span and adding through a possibly-NULL polynomial pointer.
A malformed hint with a non-monotonic or out-of-range limit is still refused exactly as the authority does; the byte values are bounded by u8 and the 256-coefficient array.
sigEncode cleanses its partial output on failure exactly as the authority (OPENSSL_cleanse over sig_len); sigDecode leaves z/hint/c_tilde writes in place on failure (all public signature data).

boundaries.mechanism: raise_with_alg diagnostic construction and allocation-extent arithmetic
residuals: The algorithm name is a static NUL-terminated params->alg; the concatenation length and the hint packet extent are now checked adds, with an impossible overflow turned into a refusal rather than a panic or wrap.
A failed capacity check in raise_with_alg would suppress the diagnostic rather than raise a malformed one; all current callers pass bounded static text.
Both delegate bounds to Packet/WPACKET; expand_mask intentionally ignores bytes after the exact gamma1 width, matching the authority.
w1_encode writes public data and does not cleanse on refusal (authority parity).

defects.class: out-of-bounds write on an unstated hint-weight precondition
defects.description: hint_bits_encode wrote each non-zero hint coefficient at data[coeff_index++] into the omega+k-byte packet. The FIPS 204 weight bound (at most omega set coefficients) was only an unchecked caller assumption: the signing caller enforces it with vector_count_ones, but the unsafe function's contract did not state it and the helper did not enforce it. A sig whose hint carried more than omega ones (for example a future in-crate caller of ossl_ml_dsa_sig_encode, or a corrupted signature object) overran the WPACKET allocation. ASan on the pre-fix body reports a stack-buffer-overflow at this write.
defects.fix: Refuse the (omega+1)th set coefficient before the write, so coeff_index < omega <= total always holds; state the weight bound in hint_bits_encode's and ossl_ml_dsa_sig_encode's contracts. Valid signatures are unchanged.
defects.regression: ml_dsa::encoders::tests::hint_encode_refuses_a_hint_over_the_weight_bound (2-byte packet, omega=1, four set coefficients); the pre-fix body (temporary working-tree revert of the guard; the base blob's write is line 1401) was rebuilt under ASan and produced 'AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow ... hint_bits_encode' at encoders.rs:1445 of that revert, and the post-fix body passes.

defects.class: out-of-bounds read / null-pointer arithmetic on a zero-length vector (authority UB not reproduced)
defects.description: hint_bits_decode derived end = p.add(k) and entered a do/while loop unconditionally. For k == 0 it read the zero-length limit span (one byte past the packet) and then wrote through a possibly-NULL polynomial pointer; p.add(0) on NULL is itself outside Rust's pointer contract. No static parameter set has k == 0, so the arm is not reachable today, but the unsafe contract permitted it.
defects.fix: Refuse k == 0 before touching the cursor or the vector, and state k >= 1 in the contract. This is a deliberate divergence from the authority's out-of-bounds access (AGENTS §17).
defects.regression: ml_dsa::encoders::tests::hint_decode_refuses_an_empty_vector (one-byte packet, empty Vector) passes post-fix; the pre-fix arm is not driven by ASan because the null-pointer step is UB rather than an ASan-detectable access, so the instrument is recorded as Miri-scope NOT_RUN.

defects.description: The hint packet extent used omega + k without a checked add, and raise_with_alg's message capacity used the three-piece length sum (pre-fix line 310) without one. Both operands are static and small, so neither can overflow on this target; the standard nevertheless requires the extent to be locally checked rather than relying on that.
defects.fix: checked_add with an error/return on overflow for both extents. Behaviour on every reachable input is identical.
defects.regression: covered by the existing ML-DSA suite and the two new controls; no overflow input exists on 64-bit targets, so no dynamic overflow control was added.
